title: Clinical Mastery: Evaluation & Management of Exotropia
summary: Exotropia represents a common form of horizontal strabismus characterized by an outward deviation of the visual axis. This guide provides a systematic approach from diagnostic workup to surgical intervention for the ophthalmologist.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Exotropia is a binocular vision anomaly where the visual axes diverge. Prevalence is roughly 1-2% of the general population. It is frequently categorized as Intermittent Exotropia (IXT), which is the most common form in children, often progressing to constant exotropia if unmanaged.

rows: Associated with profound unilateral vision loss

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Referral
content: Acute onset in adulthood (Rule out CN III palsy/Myasthenia)
Restrictive features on forced duction testing

content.explanation: C-Cover test (unilateral), O-Observe fixation, V-Visual acuity, E-Eye movements (ductions/versions), R-Refraction (cycloplegic)

sections.title: Investigation Protocol
content: Step 1: Distance and Near Cover Testing (with best correction).
Step 2: Prism Adaptation Test to assess surgical dosage.
Step 3: Cycloplegic refraction (Essential to rule out pseudo-exotropia).
Step 5: Sensory testing (Worth 4-Dot at distance and near).

sections.title: Management Hierarchy
content: Observation: For small, asymptomatic angles (<15 prism diopters).
Optical: Minus-lens therapy to stimulate accommodative convergence.
Orthoptics: Convergence exercises for CI-type exotropia.
Surgical: Bilateral Lateral Rectus Recession (BLR) or Unilateral Resection-Recession (R&R).
Botulinum Toxin: Emerging role for small-angle overcorrections.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always perform testing at both 6 meters and 33 centimeters.
Dissociate the eyes using a prolonged cover test (30-60 min) to reveal the full angle.
In Divergence Excess, the distance deviation is >10 prism diopters larger than near deviation.
Early surgery is preferred in patients losing stereopsis.
